title: Computer Vision
intro: Learn how computers see images with deep learning: CNNs, transfer learning, YOLO object detection, segmentation, vision transformers and CLIP. It is for people who have done the Deep Learning roadmap and can train a small network in PyTorch. Two Stanford CS231n lectures frame the field and the classic CNN architectures from AlexNet to ResNet, and short explainers cover convolutions, data augmentation, U-Net and Segment Anything. In between you build a CNN classifier in PyTorch, fine-tune a pretrained network, and train a YOLO detector on your own data in Google Colab. It ends with vision transformers and CLIP, which links images and text. It takes about 4 hours 40 minutes of video.
tagline: Teach machines to see: CNNs, transfer learning, YOLO detection, segmentation, ViT, and CLIP.
prereqs: Deep Learning. Hardware: step 8 trains on a free Colab GPU; a GPU also helps if you run SAM from the step 10 repo.
